title: Geometric Proof of cos(A - B) Using the Law of Cosines on the Unit Circle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider a triangle OPQ inscribed in the unit circle with one vertex at the origin O(0, 0) and the other two vertices at P(\cos A, \sin A) and Q(\cos B, \sin B) on the unit circle, so that sides OP = 1 and OQ = 1 subtend the central angle A - B. Apply the Law of Cosines and the distance formula to triangle OPQ to derive the identity \cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B.

steps.title: Express PQ^2 Using the Law of Cosines on Triangle OPQ
steps.explanation: In triangle OPQ, the two radii have lengths OP = 1 and OQ = 1 and the included angle between the rays is A - B. Applying the Law of Cosines gives PQ^2 = 2 - 2*cos(A - B).
steps.why: By the Law of Cosines, c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab*cos(C) for any triangle.

steps.title: Express PQ^2 Using the Euclidean Distance Formula
steps.mathExpression: PQ^2 = (\cos A - \cos B)^2 + (\sin A - \sin B)^2 = (\cos^2 A + \sin^2 A) + (\cos^2 B + \sin^2 B) - 2(\cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B)
steps.explanation: Compute the squared distance between P(cos A, sin A) and Q(cos B, sin B) in the Cartesian plane and expand the binomial squares.
steps.why: The squared distance between (x_1, y_1) and (x_2, y_2) is (x_1 - x_2)^2 + (y_1 - y_2)^2.

steps.title: Simplify Using the Pythagorean Identity and Equate Both Expressions for PQ^2
steps.mathExpression: 2 - 2\cos(A - B) = 2 - 2(\cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B) \implies \cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B
steps.explanation: Since cos^2 A + sin^2 A = 1 and cos^2 B + sin^2 B = 1, the distance formula simplifies to 2 - 2(cos A cos B + sin A sin B). Equating this to 2 - 2*cos(A - B), subtracting 2, and dividing by -2 yields the identity.
steps.why: Two expressions for the same geometric length squared must be equal.
